business-logic.resolution: Port the cited paragraphs; the skeleton names the COBOL lines and the facts they touch.
business-logic.title: Business logic to port

commarea-mismatch.resolution: For each caller, confirm which layout the callee reads (the COBOL MOVEs into DFHCOMMAREA say); map that caller's record onto the DTO, or give the callee one DTO per entry.
commarea-mismatch.title: COMMAREA layout mismatches

configuration.resolution: Point the datasource at the target database; the password comes from SPRING_DATASOURCE_PASSWORD at run time, never from a file.
configuration.title: Target configuration

db2-dialect.resolution: Run each statement on the target database; DB2-only syntax (FETCH FIRST, WITH UR, special registers) needs its equivalent.
db2-dialect.title: DB2 SQL on another database

db2-positioned.resolution: Rewrite the UPDATE / DELETE to the row's key: JDBC keeps no cursor position here.
db2-positioned.title: Positioned SQL (WHERE CURRENT OF)

missing-layout.resolution: Add the missing copybook / %INCLUDE member or record to the repository and re-run; the DTO then gets its real fields.
missing-layout.title: Unresolved layouts

queue-name.resolution: Resolve the name (the MOVEs into the operand, or the installation's symbol table) and pass it: the port takes any queue name.
queue-name.title: Data-driven queue names

record-variant.resolution: Map the program's record onto the entity's fields (or split the entity); the two layouts' sizes are in the TODO.
record-variant.title: Programs reading another record layout

unchecked-resp.resolution: Decide what a failed call does: the COBOL ignores it, so the Java throws; catch it where the old behaviour (carry on) is really wanted.
unchecked-resp.title: CICS responses the COBOL never tests
